explainer.title: How it works
explainer.intro: SeBolig shows you your own data from findbolig.nu. To do that, SeBolig has to use your findbolig.nu account on your behalf. Here is what that means in practice.

password.title: What happens to your password
password.p1: When you connect your account, SeBolig sends your email and password to findbolig.nu – exactly as when you use findbolig.nu yourself.
password.p2: Afterwards SeBolig keeps your password encrypted in your own browser. It is used for one thing only: renewing your findbolig session when it expires, so you do not have to type it again.
password.p3: The password is never sent to anyone but findbolig.nu.

notStored.title: What we do not store
notStored.p1: Nothing on our servers. SeBolig has no database of users, passwords or housing data. The server forwards your requests to findbolig.nu and forgets them again.

why.title: Why we need your password
why.p1: findbolig.nu offers no way to give an app like SeBolig access without your password – not via MitID, not via a “continue with” button, and not via any official app access. We checked. The only way in is the same one you use yourself.

revoke.title: How to take access back
revoke.p1: Disconnect in SeBolig. Everything SeBolig stored on this device is erased – including the encrypted password.
revoke.p2: Change your password on findbolig.nu. SeBolig can then no longer get into your account, and the connection ends by itself.
revoke.p3: Do nothing for 30 days. The connection expires automatically.

device.title: Your data on this device
device.p1: Your appointments, offers and waiting lists are fetched from findbolig.nu through our server, but are kept only on the device you use, so they can be shown without a network too.
device.p2: A connection is per device and browser. Disconnecting on your phone leaves your computer connected – and the other way round.
device.p3: When you disconnect, all of it is erased.

who.title: Who runs this
who.p1: SeBolig.nu is an independent project and is not affiliated with findbolig.nu or DEAS.
who.p2: The code is open. You can read it and ask questions on GitHub.
